--- title: "GVC decompositions of gross exports" --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} source("analysis/_setup.R") ``` ::: All four GVC decompositions in `ddec` answer one question: *where does the value embodied in a country's gross exports come from, and how much of it is double counted?* They all start from the same Leontief inverse $B = (I - A)^{-1}$, which `load_icio()` computes once. | Function | Reference | Level | Terms | |---|---|---|---:| | `leontief()` | @hummels2001 | country-industry origin | domestic / foreign content | | `kww()` | @koopman2014 | country | 9 | | `wwz()` | @wang2013 | bilateral country-industry | 16 | | `bm()` | @borin2019; @belotti2021 | country / sector / bilateral | up to 13 | ## Data We use two tables. `leather` is the small 3-country × 3-industry example shipped with the package (Argentina, Turkey, Germany). `icio_synth` holds two **synthetic** 3 × 2 tables ("2010" and "2020") generated by `simulate_icio()`. Between the two years the foreign input share goes up and value-added coefficients go down, so the second table has deeper global value chains. Its numbers have no empirical meaning (see `data-raw/get_icio_data.R`). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_leather <- load_icio(leather) m_synth <- lapply(icio_synth, load_icio) ``` ::: ## All four methods on one table `gvc_components()` runs every method on the same `icio` object and maps their terms onto common categories: * **VAX**: domestic value added absorbed abroad * **REF**: domestic value added that returns home * **DDC** and **FDC**: domestic and foreign double counting * **FVA**: foreign value added The Leontief/HIY method does not separate value added from double counting. It splits exports into domestic content (DC) and foreign content (FC) only. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- gvc_components(m_leather) tab <- dcast(g[, .(value = sum(value)), by = .(method, Exporting_Country, category)], Exporting_Country + method ~ category, value.var = "value", fill = NA) setcolorder(tab, c("Exporting_Country", "method", "VAX", "REF", "DDC", "FVA", "FDC", "DC", "FC")) tab[, GEXP := rowSums(.SD, na.rm = TRUE), .SDcols = -(1:2)] tab[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) round(x, 3) else x)] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|Exporting_Country |method | VAX| REF| DDC| FVA| FDC| DC| FC| GEXP| |:-----------------|:--------|------:|------:|-----:|------:|-----:|-------:|------:|-----:| |Argentina |leontief | NA| NA| NA| NA| NA| 53.690| 10.610| 64.3| |Argentina |kww | 46.732| 6.085| 0.872| 6.839| 3.771| NA| NA| 64.3| |Argentina |wwz | 46.732| 6.085| 0.872| 6.839| 3.771| NA| NA| 64.3| |Argentina |bm | 46.732| 6.085| 0.872| 10.435| 0.175| NA| NA| 64.3| |Turkey |leontief | NA| NA| NA| NA| NA| 92.462| 21.138| 113.6| |Turkey |kww | 77.341| 12.483| 2.637| 15.565| 5.573| NA| NA| 113.6| |Turkey |wwz | 77.341| 12.483| 2.637| 15.565| 5.573| NA| NA| 113.6| |Turkey |bm | 77.341| 12.483| 2.637| 20.556| 0.583| NA| NA| 113.6| |Germany |leontief | NA| NA| NA| NA| NA| 111.291| 36.309| 147.6| |Germany |kww | 96.719| 10.123| 4.448| 31.124| 5.185| NA| NA| 147.6| |Germany |wwz | 96.719| 10.123| 4.448| 31.124| 5.185| NA| NA| 147.6| |Germany |bm | 96.719| 10.123| 4.448| 35.065| 1.245| NA| NA| 147.6|
::: ::: ### Adding-up check Every method's components must sum to gross exports. The package tests this at 1e-8 for every level and table. Here is the check on `leather`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gexp <- data.table(Exporting_Country = m_leather$k, GEXP = tapply(m_leather$E, rep(m_leather$k, each = m_leather$N), sum)[m_leather$k]) chk <- merge(g[, .(sum_components = sum(value)), by = .(method, Exporting_Country)], gexp, by = "Exporting_Country") chk[, max_abs_error := abs(sum_components - GEXP)] chk[, .(max_abs_error = max(max_abs_error)), by = method] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|method | max_abs_error| |:--------|-------------:| |leontief | 0| |kww | 0| |wwz | 0| |bm | 0|
::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cats <- c("VAX", "REF", "DDC", "FVA", "FDC", "DC", "FC") gp <- g[, .(value = sum(value)), by = .(method, Exporting_Country, category)] gp[, category := factor(category, levels = rev(cats))] ggplot(gp, aes(x = method, y = value, fill = category)) + geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) + facet_wrap(~Exporting_Country, nrow = 1) + scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(pal[1:7], cats), breaks = cats) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Gross exports (table units)", title = "Four decompositions of the same gross exports", subtitle = "Domestic categories (VAX, REF, DDC, DC) at the bottom; foreign (FVA, FDC, FC) on top") + guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Gross exports by component, method and country (`leather` table). VAX, REF and DDC agree across KWW, WWZ and BM. KWW and WWZ shift foreign value added into foreign double counting compared with BM, which is the bias Borin and Mancini (2019) correct. Leontief/HIY gives only domestic vs foreign content; its domestic content equals VAX + REF + DDC exactly.](01-gvc-decomposition_files/figure-html/fig-gvc-1.png){#fig-gvc width=768} ::: ::: ## The KWW bias KWW and WWZ agree with BM on all the domestic terms. The difference is how foreign content is split between value added (FVA) and double counting (FDC). The corrected KWW decomposition, `bm(perspective = "world", approach = "sink")`, fixes this. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fc <- g[content == "foreign", .(value = sum(value)), by = .(method, Exporting_Country, category)] dcast(fc[method != "leontief"], Exporting_Country + category ~ method, value.var = "value")[ , lapply(.SD, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) round(x, 3) else x)] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|Exporting_Country |category | kww| wwz| bm| |:-----------------|:--------|------:|------:|------:| |Argentina |FDC | 3.771| 3.771| 0.175| |Argentina |FVA | 6.839| 6.839| 10.435| |Turkey |FDC | 5.573| 5.573| 0.583| |Turkey |FVA | 15.565| 15.565| 20.556| |Germany |FDC | 5.185| 5.185| 1.245| |Germany |FVA | 31.124| 31.124| 35.065|
::: ::: ## Bilateral and sector level WWZ and BM also work at the bilateral level. Their bilateral results sum back to the country totals: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gb <- gvc_components(m_leather, methods = c("wwz", "bm"), level = "bilateral") head(dcast(gb[, .(value = sum(value)), by = .(method, Exporting_Country, Importing_Country, category)], method + Exporting_Country + Importing_Country ~ category, value.var = "value"), 8) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|method |Exporting_Country |Importing_Country | DDC| FDC| FVA| REF| VAX| |:------|:-----------------|:-----------------|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|--------:| |wwz |Argentina |Turkey | 0.2623381| 1.2074658| 2.029392| 1.829216| 16.37159| |wwz |Argentina |Germany | 0.6100568| 2.5633658| 4.809820| 4.256258| 30.36050| |wwz |Turkey |Argentina | 0.3683927| 0.7001959| 3.793686| 1.023445| 18.51428| |wwz |Turkey |Germany | 2.2685436| 4.8729669| 11.771398| 11.459929| 58.82716| |wwz |Germany |Argentina | 1.5545079| 1.6437779| 12.581345| 3.100081| 37.92029| |wwz |Germany |Turkey | 2.8936721| 3.5416232| 18.542671| 7.023180| 58.79885| |bm |Argentina |Turkey | 0.2723248| 0.0551900| 3.181668| 1.829216| 16.36160| |bm |Argentina |Germany | 0.6000701| 0.1200163| 7.253169| 4.256258| 30.37049|
::: ```{.r .cell-code} all.equal(gb[, sum(value), by = .(method, Exporting_Country)]$V1, g[method %in% c("wwz", "bm"), sum(value), by = .(method, Exporting_Country)]$V1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Mean relative difference: 0.3309495" ``` ::: ::: ## GVC deepening in the synthetic tables ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gs <- rbindlist(lapply(names(m_synth), function(y) gvc_components(m_synth[[y]], methods = "bm")[, year := y])) dcast(gs[, .(value = sum(value)), by = .(year, Exporting_Country, category)], Exporting_Country + year ~ category, value.var = "value")[ , lapply(.SD, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) round(x, 2) else x)] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|Exporting_Country |year | DDC| FDC| FVA| REF| VAX| |:-----------------|:----|----:|----:|-----:|-----:|------:| |C1 |2010 | 1.10| 0.17| 14.91| 7.42| 91.43| |C1 |2020 | 6.65| 1.97| 47.47| 16.01| 144.26| |C2 |2010 | 1.11| 0.17| 15.67| 6.82| 96.74| |C2 |2020 | 6.19| 1.85| 46.18| 17.78| 137.12| |C3 |2010 | 1.14| 0.17| 17.12| 6.43| 106.26| |C3 |2020 | 5.87| 1.76| 46.31| 19.74| 134.41|
::: ::: Foreign value added (FVA) increases in every country between 2010 and 2020. [Structural parallels](03-structural-parallels.qmd) decomposes the change in domestic content into technology, value-added and export effects, and checks that the decomposition does not depend on the order of the factors.
